questions.question_text: (i) What is UNIX? (ii) Which command shows current directory? (iii) Which of the following is a relative path? (iv) What is the function of PATH variable? (v) Which symbol represents parent directory?
questions.model_answer:
(i) Operating system
(ii) pwd
(iii) Documents
(iv) Stores command search directories
(v) ..

key_points.description: (ii) Which command shows current directory?: pwd
(iii) Which of the following is a relative path?: Documents
(iv) What is the function of PATH variable?: Stores command search directories

questions.question_text: (i) Define Kernel. (ii) What is a shell? (iii) What is a directory? (iv) What is login prompt? (v) What is POSIX?
questions.model_answer: (i) Kernel is the core of the OS. (ii) Shell is the command interpreter. (iii) Directory is a folder for files. (iv) Login prompt is the interface for user authentication. (v) POSIX is a standard for OS compatibility.

key_points.description: (i) Define Kernel: Kernel is the core of the OS
(ii) What is a shell?: Shell is the command interpreter
(iii) What is a directory?: Directory is a folder for files
(iv) What is login prompt?: Login prompt is the interface for user authentication
(v) What is POSIX?: POSIX is a standard for OS compatibility

questions.model_answer: UNIX architecture consists of the hardware at the center, surrounded by the kernel, then the shell, and finally the user applications.

key_points.description: Explanation of Shell and User interaction

questions.question_text: Write any four features of UNIX with examples.
questions.model_answer: Features include multi-user, multi-tasking, hierarchical file system, and portability.

questions.question_text: Differentiate between internal and external commands.
questions.model_answer: Internal commands are built into the shell, while external commands are separate executable files.

questions.question_text: Explain absolute path and relative path with examples.
questions.model_answer: Absolute path starts from root (/), relative path starts from current directory.

questions.question_text: Explain pwd, cd and ls commands with examples.
questions.model_answer: pwd prints working directory, cd changes directory, ls lists files.

questions.question_text: What is UNIX file system? Explain its structure.
questions.model_answer: The UNIX file system is a hierarchical tree structure starting from the root directory.

questions.question_text: Explain the working of UNIX environment. Also explain environment variables with examples.
questions.model_answer: The UNIX environment manages user sessions and processes. Environment variables store configuration data like PATH.

questions.question_text: Explain the following commands with examples: 1) Echo 2) printf 3) who 4) date 5) cal. Explain directory management in UNIX. Write commands for creating, navigating and deleting directories.
questions.model_answer: Commands: echo prints text, printf formats output, who shows users, date shows time, cal shows calendar. Directory management uses mkdir, cd, and rmdir.

key_points.description: (v) cal. Explain directory management in UNIX. Write commands for creating, navigating and deleting directories
